articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
articles.summary:
Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next

A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.

Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors peered down on the scene.

articles.title: ‘I spent five years with criminals’: dissident Cuban artist embraces new life in US after prison release
articles.summary:
Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara tells of the reality of prison, drinking whisky with his captors, and being painted by George W Bush

When Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara was pushed into the back of a police car on 11 July 2021, during the biggest protests Cuba had seen in nearly three decades, he expected to be in custody for “one, maybe two days”. Instead five years would pass before he was free, and only then after he’d agreed to exile.

“I remember that Sunday,” he says as he opens a beer in El Espacio 23, an art gallery in the Allapattah neighbourhood of Miami. “I was at my girlfriend’s. Friends started writing to tell me there were demonstrations in the streets. It felt like the day we all longed for had arrived – the end of the dictatorship – and I went out into the street.”

archive.security_status_cs: Jižní Amerika čelí stupňujícímu se napětí v souvislosti s těsným druhým kolem prezidentských voleb v Brazílii, kde se Lula a Bolsonaro utkávají v ostrém statistickém souboji. Rostoucí ceny ropy (Brent nad 110 USD) a kolísavé ceny komodit podtrhují makroekonomickou nestabilitu, zatímco regionální bezpečnost nadále zatěžují silné drogové kartely a přetrvávající potíže s organizovaným zločinem v Ekvádoru a Kolumbii. Argentinské diplomatické manévry vůči Falklandským ostrovům a napětí v energetickém sektoru navíc zvyšují geopolitické třeně.
archive.security_status_en: South America faces mounting tension surrounding the neck-and-neck presidential runoff in Brazil, where Lula and Bolsonaro are locked in a statistical dead heat. Surging oil prices (Brent above $110) and volatile commodity markets underscore macroeconomic instability, while regional security remains pressured by powerful drug cartels and persistent organized crime challenges in Ecuador and Colombia. Additionally, Argentine diplomatic maneuvers over the Falkland Islands and energy sector friction are amplifying geopolitical risks.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, expect the climax of the campaign and the execution of Brazil's presidential runoff, which will dictate the future direction of Latin American markets. The impact of expensive oil on regional inflation expectations will also be closely watched.

archive.security_status_cs: V Jižní Americe nadále dominují vyhrocené prezidentské volby v Brazílii mezi Luizou Ináciem Lulou da Silva a opozicí, doprovázené prudkými politickými střety a rekordně nízkou odlesněností Amazonie. Mezitím Argentina zostřuje rétoriku vůči Spojenému království kvůli Falklandám a ohrožuje ropné či rybářské projekty, zatímco bezpečnostní situace v Ekvádoru a Kolumbii zůstává napjatá kvůli organizovanému zločinu a aktivitám kartelů.
archive.security_status_en: South America remains dominated by the fiercely contested Brazilian presidential runoff between Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and the opposition, accompanied by sharp political clashes and record-low Amazon deforestation. Meanwhile, Argentina is escalating rhetoric against the UK over the Falklands, threatening oil and fishing projects, while security in Ecuador and Colombia remains heavily strained by organized crime and cartel activities.
